entry.title: Cyber resilience: building confidence as threats evolve
entry.summary: Cyber resilience: building confidence as threats evolve FCA · Nov 27, 2026 · SpeechMark Francis, director of specialists at the FCA, gave a speech at a financial services cyber security summit. He argues that faster, more accessible and more interconnected threats make cyber fundamentals more important, and that boards need an honest view of their resilience. He notes that the FCA, Bank of England and PRA opened a consultation on proposed cyber resilience guidance that brings together existing requirements rather than introducing new rules. He also urges firms to prepare early for quantum computing risks. The archived text and attachments run to about 12,720 characters; the summary is based only on the first 12,000. Check the original.

entry.title: UK regulators complete 2026 annual review of payments Memorandum of Understanding
entry.summary: Authorities complete 2026 review of payments Memorandum of Understanding FCA · Nov 26, 2026 · ReportThe Bank of England, FCA, PRA and PSR completed their annual review of the payments Memorandum of Understanding. The review found cooperation among the authorities has strengthened and remains effective, so no changes to the MoU are needed. The authorities also updated information on each regulator's remit. entry.title: Correction to data used in motor finance compensation calculation
entry.summary: Motor finance compensation scheme calculation FCA · Nov 26, 2026 · GuidanceThe FCA says it found errors in how it categorised a small group of loan agreements while preparing its response to legal challenges to its motor finance redress scheme. The data informed the APR adjustment of 17% used for agreements from 1 April 2014. Initial work suggests any impact would be less than 1 percentage point either side of 17%, with average compensation affected by less than £10 per agreement. Two challengers are due to serve expert evidence on 27 November 2026, and the timeline will be discussed with them and the court.

entry.title: Check the firm before investing: FCA warns as AI investment scams rise
entry.summary: Check the firm before you invest, FCA warns, as AI scams rise FCA · Nov 26, 2026 · EnforcementA new FCA survey found that a third of UK adults saw an investment promotion in the past year that they believe used AI. Reports of investment fraud mentioning suspected AI use rose by nearly 400% in a year. The FCA urges people to use its Firm Checker to confirm a firm is authorised before investing. entry.title: How should investors evaluate fund performance?
entry.summary: How should investors evaluate performance? FCA · Nov 25, 2026 · GuidanceThe UK Financial Conduct Authority advises investors not to judge a fund only by whether its headline return beats a benchmark. Instead, investors should check the fund's stated objective, strategy and style, and whether it still fits their wider portfolio. The document notes that when a few large companies dominate markets, a more diversified fund may lag a concentrated index without the manager having made poor decisions. It also says style biases should be clearly disclosed and that managers must assess fund value annually.

entry.title: Smarter regulation means weighing trade-offs
entry.summary: Smarter regulation means understanding the trade-offs FCA · Nov 24, 2026 · SpeechThe UK Financial Conduct Authority reports on its annual Economics Conference, where speakers discussed how evidence-based economic analysis can make financial regulation proportionate while supporting growth and innovation. The article argues that regulators should weigh costs against benefits and test whether interventions work in practice rather than assume they do. It also invites researchers to suggest topics for further study.

entry.title: Notice that Kandoo Car Credit Ltd has entered administration
entry.summary: Kandoo Car Credit Ltd enters administration FCA · Nov 23, 2026 · EnforcementKandoo Car Credit Ltd, a UK motor finance credit broker, entered administration on 23 November 2026, with Steve Kenny and Richard Cole of KBL Advisory Ltd appointed as joint administrators. Kandoo is no longer arranging finance, and existing agreements are with the lender, so customers should keep making repayments to them. Claims against Kandoo itself go to the joint administrators, while scheme compensation is the lender's responsibility.

entry.title: Bereaved families need support rather than a struggle with paperwork
entry.summary: Bereaved families need support, not a battle with paperwork FCA · Nov 23, 2026 · ReportThe FCA reviewed how financial advisers, wealth managers and investment platforms support bereaved families and those handling estates. It found confusing communications, delays and gaps in support, and some firms still charged advice fees until an original death certificate was provided. The FCA says firms should explain next steps in plain English, offer several ways to report a death, keep paperwork proportionate and stop ongoing advice fees where the service is no longer provided.

entry.title: Reality TV star and unauthorised finfluencer sentenced for illegally promoting high-risk investments on social media
entry.summary: Geordie Shore star and illegal finfluencer sentenced for promoting high-risk investments on social media FCA · Nov 19, 2026 · EnforcementThe FCA announced that reality TV star Aaron Chalmers and finfluencer Jason Agbodza were sentenced for illegally promoting an unauthorised forex trading scheme on social media. Both pleaded guilty and were fined and ordered to pay costs at City of London Magistrates Court. The FCA also urges social media platforms to do more to stop illegal financial promotions at source.

entry.title: FCA and Financial Ombudsman urge insurers to improve claims handling
entry.summary: Insurance firms called on to improve claims handling FCA · Nov 19, 2026 · ReportThe FCA and Financial Ombudsman Service have published a joint report on what insurers should focus on so that claims are handled promptly, clearly and fairly. It calls on insurers to keep claims moving, give customers clear and timely updates, and take responsibility when third parties working for them cause problems. The report notes that 79% of people who make a claim are satisfied with claims handling. The archived text and attachments run to about 189,398 characters; the summary is based only on the first 12,000. Check the original.

entry.title: Speech by FCA deputy chief executive on the courage to change innovation regulation
entry.summary: The courage to change FCA · Nov 19, 2026 · SpeechSarah Pritchard, deputy chief executive of the UK Financial Conduct Authority, gave this speech at the TheCityUK National Conference 2026 in Bristol. She argues that regulators and firms must challenge established thinking and accept uncertainty to sustain fintech growth. The speech describes the FCA's Innovation Services, Regulatory Sandbox, AI Lab and AI Spotlight Observatory, and invites firms to engage early with their ideas.

entry.title: UK financial regulators propose cyber guidance as attacks rise
entry.summary: UK financial watchdogs clarify cyber expectations as attacks rise FCA · Nov 19, 2026 · Draft / consultationThe FCA, PRA and Bank of England have jointly proposed guidance to help financial firms prepare for and recover from cyber incidents, without imposing rigid rules. The guidance aligns with the NCSC's Cyber Assessment Framework and covers governance, identification, protection, detection, response and recovery. The consultation closes on 26 February 2027.

entry.title: UK regulator launches public platform showing how firms use AI in financial services
entry.summary: FCA launches world-first platform giving firms new insight into AI innovation FCA · Nov 19, 2026The FCA has launched the AI Spotlight Observatory, a world-first online platform showing real-world AI use cases from more than 200 organisations across 150 areas of activity. It highlights trends in tools for financial crime and compliance, as well as emerging technologies such as agentic payments and neurosymbolic AI. The platform is open to all, with registration needed for detailed insights and direct contact with featured innovators, and firms can apply to be showcased.

entry.title: Helping more people break the cycle of persistent credit card debt
entry.summary: Helping more people break the cycle of persistent credit card debt FCA · Nov 18, 2026 · ReportThe FCA evaluated its 2018 persistent debt rules for credit cards. It found that the share of accounts in persistent debt fell from 7% to 3% between 2018 and early 2023, and many customers changed their repayments after being contacted. The FCA notes that changing economic conditions mean it cannot conclude the rules alone caused these improvements.

entry.title: UK financial regulator charges an individual with money laundering
entry.summary: FCA charges individual with money laundering FCA · Nov 17, 2026 · EnforcementThe FCA has charged Raymond Fieldhouse with money laundering. He is accused of laundering over £1.42m from investment scams between June 2017 and August 2018. He appeared at Stockport Magistrates' Court on 17 November 2026, entered no plea, and was remanded in custody until a hearing on 22 December 2026 at Southwark Crown Court.

entry.title: Full view of UK share trading across venues
entry.summary: Getting the full picture of trading in UK shares FCA · Nov 17, 2026 · GuidanceThe FCA notes that UK share trading is now spread across more venues and execution methods, so data focused on traditional venues may understate total activity. It launched a market activity reporter that brings together trading data from across UK execution venues and methods. The service now also provides FTSE 100 and FTSE 250 level data.

entry.title: UK FCA: trends seen in firms applying to its innovation services
entry.summary: What we’re learning from firms engaging with our innovation services FCA · Nov 17, 2026 · ReportThe Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) summarises trends from applications to its Regulatory Sandbox and Innovation Pathways. In 2026, 37% of applications involved AI, up from 31% in 2025, and 92% of firms were using the services for the first time. About 70% of applicants were 0 to 2 years old. The article also describes a stablecoins cohort and a climate scenarios cohort that opened applications on 1 October 2026. entry.title: FCA proposes exempting performance fees from workplace pension default fund charge cap
entry.summary: FCA proposes greater pension investment flexibility to support long-term value for savers FCA · Nov 12, 2026 · Draft / consultationThe FCA is consulting on excluding certain performance-linked fees from the charge cap for default funds in workplace pensions, giving providers more flexibility to invest in private markets for long-term returns. The proposals include safeguards on transparency, fair allocation of fees between savers, and scrutiny of how private assets are valued. The consultation closes on 14 January 2027, and the FCA expects to make final rules in summer 2027.

entry.title: Man sentenced for fake £154m takeover bid targeting UK-listed company
entry.summary: Man sentenced over £154m fake takeover bid targeting UK-listed company FCA · Nov 10, 2026 · EnforcementThe FCA announced that Christopher Woolcott received a 2-year prison sentence, suspended for 2 years, plus 200 hours of unpaid work and costs for staging a fake takeover bid for Touchstone Exploration Inc. He invented several identities, forged takeover documents and met the chief executive under a false name. The aim was to drive up the share price and profit from selling his shares.

entry.title: Start your Self Assessment tax return early before the 31 January deadline
entry.summary: Stay on top of your finances, start your Self Assessment today HMRC / gov.uk · Nov 10, 2026 · GuidanceHMRC encourages Self Assessment customers to start their tax return for the 2025 to 2026 tax year now, as the filing and payment deadline is 31 January 2027. Returns can be filed and tax paid online via GOV.UK or the HMRC app. The notice also says UK cryptoasset owners must pay Capital Gains Tax on gains above the £3,000 allowance and declare them in their Self Assessment return.</summary>
